premise: Beetle crawls into the open magnolia for a cosy nap in the sun, wakes up yellow all over with pollen, and Flower asks him to carry it to the magnolia across the valley, where it will help make seeds; off he flies, proud, and Berry Bush winks.
inspiration: Kipling's 'Just So' 'how' pattern, true version: how a magnolia makes its seeds — with a sleepy beetle's help.
lesson: Even a nap can turn into a good deed.
learning: Beetles visit magnolia flowers and carry their pollen from one flower to the next.

en-US.title: Beetle and the Magnolia
en-US.text: {flower:enter} {bush:enter} {canvas:sunshine 0.7} The sun was warm on the valley, and Flower {flower:live open hold} opened her petals wide. {beetle:enter} Beetle came trundling through the grass. {beetle:face happy} "What a cosy spot!" {beetle:go on flower} He climbed right into the middle of the flower, snuggled down in the soft yellow dust, {beetle:live sleep hold} and fell fast asleep. {sfx:snore} {bush:face happy} Berry Bush smiled. [whispers] "Shh, everyone." When Beetle woke up, {beetle:live sleep resume} he stretched and blinked {beetle:face surprised} and looked at himself. He was {beetle:sparkle #FFD84A} yellow all over! Yellow legs, yellow feelers, a yellow shiny shell. [curious] "Is this your dust?" {flower:sparkle #FFD84A} "It's my pollen," said Flower. "Will you take some to the magnolia across the valley? It helps her make seeds." {beetle:face happy} "A job for me!" {beetle:live shine} Beetle puffed up proudly. Then {beetle:live open-wings} he lifted his shiny shell, out came his wings, {sfx:whirr} whirr, {beetle:go away by fly} and off he flew, far across the valley, dusty and proud. {bush:live wink} Berry Bush winked at Flower. [warmly] "The sleepiest helper in the valley," he said, {flower:hearts} "and the best."

es-ES.title: El escarabajo y la magnolia
es-ES.text: {flower:enter} {bush:enter} {canvas:sunshine 0.7} El sol calentaba el valle, y Flor {flower:live open hold} abrió sus pétalos de par en par. {beetle:enter} Escarabajo llegó caminando entre la hierba. {beetle:face happy} —¡Qué sitio tan calentito! {beetle:go on flower} Se metió en el centro de la flor, se acurrucó en el polvillo amarillo {beetle:live sleep hold} y se quedó frito. {sfx:snore} {bush:face happy} Arbusto de bayas sonrió. [whispers] —Chist, no hagáis ruido. Cuando Escarabajo se despertó, {beetle:live sleep resume} se estiró, parpadeó {beetle:face surprised} y se miró. ¡Estaba {beetle:sparkle #FFD84A} amarillo de arriba abajo! Patas amarillas, antenas amarillas y el caparazón brillante, amarillo también. [curious] —¿Esto es tu polvillo? {flower:sparkle #FFD84A} —Es mi polen —dijo Flor—. ¿Le llevarías un poco a la magnolia del otro lado del valle? Así podrá hacer semillas. {beetle:face happy} —¡Un trabajo para mí! {beetle:live shine} Escarabajo se hinchó de orgullo. Luego {beetle:live open-wings} levantó su caparazón, desplegó las alas y, {sfx:whirr} brrrr, {beetle:go away by fly} allá se fue volando, cubierto de polen y muy orgulloso. {bush:live wink} Arbusto le guiñó un ojo a Flor. [warmly] —El ayudante más dormilón del valle —dijo—. {flower:hearts} Y el mejor.
